correctness.rationale: The independent triples of K_m square P_3 are exactly A_i B_j C_k with i!=j and k!=j. At fixed B,C missing indices Q,R, the available A subsets form an empty fiber if |J|=0, a cone freely toggled at A_j when |J|=1, or full simplex boundary if |J|>=2; sequential A_0 toggling then leaves the A_1..A_m−1 face. For |R|>=2 the B fiber is the (m−3)-skeleton and its B_0 matching leaves m−1 subsets of B_1..; singleton R gives a free cone coordinate. C skeleton similarly leaves m−1 subsets. The complete acyclic sequential matching therefore has exactly (m−1)² critical (3m−6)-cells and the empty face is matched. For m>=3, one basepoint plus only these higher-dimensional cells yields wedge of spheres; m=2 gives S0. Independently built graph adjacency and all complex faces and rematched at m=2,3,4: face counts 15,298,3247, matched pairs 7,147,1619, critical 1,4,9 with predicted exact masks. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace the all-m fiber argument.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS: published Conjecture 4.3 already predicts the exact reduced homology for n=3, so the Betti-number formula alone is not novel. The uniform all-m acyclic matching and integral homotopy sphere wedge instead provide proof and strengthen the conjecture. Broader published total-two-cut results and tables do not settle this total-three-cut slice.
residual_risks: A later unindexed full proof of Conjecture 4.3 for arbitrary path length might dominate this slice; no such theorem was established in the searches.
Finite m=2..4 checks corroborate but do not establish the infinitely many widths; the proof depends on the symbolic fiber-matching classification.

value.rationale: A uniform integral homotopy classification of the first arbitrary-width n=3 slice settles an explicit published homology conjecture for infinitely many m and strengthens it to a sphere wedge. This is motivated by an open named family, not a re-tabulation of finitely checked cases.
